clue.text: Still agog

definitions.meaning: air with no wind at all is described this way, as on a hot motionless day
someone agog is gasping with eager anticipation, hardly able to inhale

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one adjective: windless weather, and a person panting with excitement.

clue.text: Turning corrupt, a politician

parts.note: to corrupt is to rot, as a verb meaning to decay morally
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician is going bad and taking bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reads as a verb describing the politician's fall, but it is an adjective defining the answer; 'corrupt' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives for something that revolves, like a spinning motion.

clue.text: Certainly organ may be heard

indicators.note: says the organ's name is to be spoken and listened to, not read

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that a church organ is audible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be heard' tells you to say the organ, EYE; the surface wants a musical organ, but it is a bodily one.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of assent, as said in a parliamentary vote or by a sailor.

clue.text: Lift first of immaculate white shrouds

indicators.note: as a verb, shrouds means wraps round, so the wine goes around the single letter

parts.note: hock is a German white wine

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone raises the first of some spotless white burial cloths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrouds' is a verb, not burial cloths: HOCK, a German white wine, wraps round the I that 'first of' takes from immaculate.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal synonym: to raise or pull something with a jerk.

clue.text: Leader in equestrianism, victory key for competitive horse

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victory, as in VE Day
Enter is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: For a horse in competition, winning is the vital thing in becoming top of the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader in' takes the E of equestrianism; 'key' is a keyboard key, not something crucial.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that takes part in three-day trials of dressage, cross-country and jumping.

clue.text: Aid sent to poor is posted

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters before it are in a bad state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Charity donations for the needy go off in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like the needy receiving the aid, but it tells you to rearrange 'Aid sent to'. 'posted' is the military sense, not the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier assigned to a place of duty is described by either word.

clue.text: Entering room in knickers, fashion victim?

indicators.note: the answer goes inside the following words, lying across them in order

explanation.surface: A slave to trends walks into a room wearing only underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entering' says the answer sits inside 'room in knickers'. The victim is literal: an animal killed for its fur.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of an animal that dies so its fur can be worn.

clue.text: Philosopher I support for a very short time

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a 19th-century English philosopher
to second a motion is to support it

explanation.surface: The speaker backs a thinker, but only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth of a second, an example of a tiny interval.

clue.text: Sweet, posh, with label attached round about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole assembly is read from its far end
this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: a tag is a label
something attached is on, as a lid is on a jar
U is the old British shorthand for upper-class usage, as opposed to non-U

explanation.surface: A charming, upper-class person has a name tag pinned on somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the label-and-attached run around the posh letter, giving TAGUON, and 'about' turns that back to front. 'Sweet' is a noun, a confection.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of sugar, egg white and nuts is an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Dull, see, their plays

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters before it move about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds a company's dramas boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' is a verb telling you to rearrange 'see their', not stage dramas. 'Dull' is a verb: to numb.
explanation.definitionFit: To anaesthetise someone with ether numbs their senses.

clue.text: Determined innings over then?

definitions.meaning: an effort made with full force and total commitment is called this
in cricket, an innings ends when ten of the batting side's eleven players have been dismissed

explanation.surface: A resolute batting spell comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase covers a full-force effort and the cricket scoreboard's term for a batting side dismissed.

clue.text: Offensive, a course inspiring thuggery primarily

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the course takes a letter inside

parts.note: a tack is a ship's course relative to the wind, or a line of approach

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A disgusting training programme encourages violence above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' means breathing in: TACK takes in the T that 'primarily' picks from thuggery. 'Offensive' is a noun, a military assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A military assault is called an offensive.

clue.text: Vehicle covered by bill sticker — that's promotion!

indicators.note: the vehicle is enclosed by the two pieces that follow, joined together

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad
cement is something that sticks things together
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van is plastered with an advertising poster as marketing.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bill sticker' is someone who pastes up posters, but the two words split into an advert and a glue, which 'covered by' wraps around the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for moving up in rank or career.

clue.text: Island: old man therein crossing river, doing the backstroke?

indicators.note: crossing means going over, so the turned letters span the river's letter
a backstroke swimmer travels backwards, so the letters are read from the far end

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
therein means in it
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An elderly man on an island swims across a river on his back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the backstroke' turns DAD IN IT into TINIDAD, and 'crossing' sets that around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island, the larger partner of Tobago.

clue.text: Hard and windblown Hindu kush, say, where shots fired repeatedly?

parts.note: driving rain is rain falling hard and blown by the wind
the Hindu Kush is a mountain range in Afghanistan and Pakistan

explanation.surface: A harsh, gale-swept mountain region is the scene of constant gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: The shots are golf shots, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where golfers practise hitting ball after ball.

clue.text: Score, might you say, that's written on

definitions.meaning: a musical score is sheets covered in notes, so whimsically it could be called this
sheets of stationery for writing letters

explanation.surface: A tally, so to speak, that has been jotted down.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing stationery, and a fanciful description of sheet music as sheets full of musical symbols.

clue.text: King and queen to stop celebs revealing all

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the royal letters go inside the celebs

parts.note: celebrities are stars
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: The royal couple intervene to prevent celebrities telling every secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' means to plug a gap, so the royal pair sit inside the celebs. The revealing is of flesh, not secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for completely naked.

clue.text: What one making a mad dash is, and does? Basic stuff

parts.words: What one making a mad dash is
parts.note: someone mad is nuts
someone making a dash bolts, runs off suddenly

explanation.surface: A riddle about a person running frantically, said to be elementary.
explanation.walkthrough: A person making a mad dash is mad and dashes: one word for each, joined by the clue's own 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the practical fundamentals of something.

clue.text: Always forgetting where Lebanon is, assuming Norway initially in middle east

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the continent takes the other letters inside

parts.note: Lebanon is a country in Asia

indicators.note: places the single letter inside the abbreviation that follows
takes the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone hopeless at geography never recalls where Lebanon is and puts Norway in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' and 'in' build MNE first, and 'assuming' has the continent take that inside. The surface's muddled geography is all wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical description of the condition of memory loss.

clue.text: Is man one, evolved?

indicators.note: something evolved has changed form, so the letters before it change their order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A question about whether humans are apes that have developed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'evolved' rearranges ISMAN plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans are primates, so a person is arguably an ape that has developed further.

clue.text: Flies disturbed sleep after turning over for quick stretch?

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters of the word before it are thrown out of order
after places this piece second, and turning over flips it end to end

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Insects wake someone, who rolls over and briefly stretches their limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges Flies, and 'after turning over' adds the sleep backwards as PAN. The stretch is a period of time, and quick is the old word for alive.
explanation.definitionFit: The period for which someone is alive, quick being an old word for living.

clue.text: Iron lady, it's felt

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: The influence of Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, is noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Lady was the nickname of British prime minister Margaret Thatcher; here the two words split. 'felt' is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft hat with a creased crown, typically made of the fabric felt.

clue.text: Given worms while in nest, possibly — had enough?

definitions.text: Given worms while in nest, possibly
definitions.meaning: a chick is given food by its parents while aloft in a tree
someone who can take no more is bored or annoyed

explanation.surface: A chick stuffed with worms by its parents wants no more.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical picture of a chick nourished high in a tree, and an idiom for being exasperated.

clue.text: Carefully consider result of enlargement?

definitions.meaning: to assess or weigh up a person or situation
when something is made bigger, its dimensions have risen

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard about how a blown-up photograph turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to assess, and a whimsical report that dimensions have increased.

clue.text: Duck, parrot and budgie, perhaps, back on team

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another is added at its end

parts.note: a side is a sports team

indicators.note: back says the pets' word is written from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a parrot and a budgie, a small British cage bird, are examples of pets

explanation.surface: Three birds have returned to join a squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PETS into STEP, and 'on' adds it to SIDE. 'Duck' is a verb, to dodge, not a third bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to dodge or evade something.

clue.text: Audibly mark offbeat music

indicators.note: the mark's word is to be spoken, giving a different spelling with the same pronunciation

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone loudly beats time to unconventional music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audibly' has you say SCAR, which in British speech has no sounded R. 'offbeat' is literal: the rhythm stresses the offbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican genre whose rhythm accents the offbeat.

clue.text: Gathering speed at sea, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a tight cluster of people standing together
a ship's speed is measured in units of one nautical mile per hour

explanation.surface: A ship is picking up pace out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for a small cluster of people and for the nautical unit of velocity.

clue.text: Value again up following overhaul of paper

indicators.note: following places this piece after the rearranged letters
an overhaul takes something apart and rebuilds it, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: to up something, such as a price or the stakes, is to raise it

explanation.surface: A newspaper's worth has risen once more after it was revamped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhaul of' rearranges paper and 'following' places the second piece after it. 'up' is a verb here, as in upping a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess the worth of something a second time.
